goal: As finance director of a Florida FQHC, reconcile FY2024 per-visit reimbursement against CMS FQHC PPS (GAF-adjusted) and Florida AHCA Medicaid PPS benchmarks in a PASS/REVIEW/FAIL CSV. Build a 4-sheet Board workbook (revenue and expense variance, HealthFirst peer ratios, service-line profitability) and a Board memo covering variances, audit findings, peer ratios, the FY2025 Medicare projection, and recommendations on Medicaid reconciliation, cost per visit, 340B feasibility and workforce costs.
delivered: FY2024_Rate_Compliance_Audit.csv with 20 rows; Medicare benchmark $196.98 = CY2025 $202.65 x GAF 0.972, Medicaid proxy $157.27. FY2024_Board_Financial_Report.xlsx with 4 sheets: the revenue sheet shows Feb Medicaid -$73,873 (-23.1%) and Jan-Mar expense overruns are flagged. FY2024_Financial_Compliance_Memo.docx with an exec summary, audit interpretation, peer section, CY2025 projection and 5-part action plan.
what_went_wrong: The agent had every needed number but made judgment and coverage choices the rubric penalized. It benchmarked FY2024 Medicare against the CY2025 rate ($202.65 x 0.972), explicitly calling the audit 'forward-looking', even though it knew CY2024 $195.99 / GAF 0.931 = $182.47. It read the full HealthFirst PDF but never computed the Note 7 contractual-adjustment rate (2,884,264 / 7,478,288 = 38.6%). The memo listed only total-revenue monthly misses, so the Feb/Mar Medicaid shortfalls (-$73,873, -$56,019), which sit in its own workbook, were never discussed with causes or tied to the Medicaid audit results. It also cited 340B $1.514M without the 17.7% share or the 55% Medicaid payer-mix argument, kept salaries and benefits separate instead of a combined 72.7% vs 65.4% personnel ratio, and did not frame Medicaid dental as structurally non-PPS.

failed_items.why: Dental/Medicaid is $91.31, FAIL (-41.9%), which is correct. However, the memo's structural caveat concerns only Medicare dental being outside PPS ('validate whether dental encounters are outside PPS scope'). Medicaid dental still gets the $157.27 facility PPS proxy with no note that it is paid at encounter- or procedure-specific rates. Borderline.

The CSV Medicare benchmark is 196.98 (CY2025 $202.65 x 0.972), and the memo says 'Medicare uses the CY2025 CMS base rate' as a 'forward-looking FY2025 audit control'. Memo §4 shows the agent knew CY2024 $195.99 x 0.931 = $182.47 but did not use the rate applicable to Oct 2023-Sep 2024 dates of service. The subagent's CY2025-focused research reinforced this.

The agent extracted all 29 PDF pages with pypdf (step 7), and Note 7 lists gross charges $7,478,288 and contractual adjustments $2,884,264. The Peer Benchmark sheet still uses only operating-revenue ratios: no 38.6% rate, no Riverside estimate, and no note that Riverside lacks gross charges.

The memo gives a 340B recommendation and cites $1.514M and $8.555M separately, but never computes the 17.7% share. It also does not discuss whether Riverside's 55% Medicaid mix supports similar 340B revenue; it says only 'should not assume comparable 340B economics'.

Salaries (57.5% vs 54.0%) and benefits (15.2% vs 11.4%) are reported only as separate rows. The combined personnel ratio of 72.7% vs HealthFirst 65.4% (+7.3 pp) is never stated. The workforce strategy sub-criterion passed.

The Revenue Variance sheet shows Feb Medicaid 246,020 vs 319,894 (-23.1%) and Mar -17.3%. The memo instead cites only total-revenue misses (Feb ($81,946) -10.5%). It gives no Medicaid-specific monthly figures, no causes (MCO payment delays, denials, retro rates), and no link to the BH/Dental Medicaid audit flags.

subagent_notes: One background subagent researched the CMS CY2025 transmittal, GAFs and the AHCA Oct-2024 schedule. Its result (base $202.65, Rest-of-Florida GAF 0.972, central-FL AHCA site rates incl. $157.27) duplicated the root's own concurrent searches but was used for the Medicaid proxy. Because it was asked only for CY2025 figures, it reinforced the CY2025-rate choice that failed R1. Otherwise neutral.
